newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Tele Danmark H1 result seen down. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Tele Danmark H1 result seen down. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark is expected to post lower first-half 1996 profits when it announces its interim result on Wednesday, an average of 10 analysts' forecasts showed on Monday.

The analysts said that their estimates were influenced by the unknown effect on Tele Danmark accounts of its new 17 percent stake in Belgian telephone company Belgacom, coupled with heavy marketing costs for its mobile telephone business.
"Tele Danmark's interim result this year is rather special in that three-month earnings from Belgacom feature on it for the first time," one analyst explained.
"Maybe Belgacom will not represent such a major outgoing as feared, as its first-half 1996 result unveiled earlier this month was better than expected," he added.

The panel forecast an average pre-tax profit for Tele Danmark of 2.205 billion crowns for the year's first six months, compared with 2.721 billion crowns for 1995's first half. The estimates ranged from 1.910 to 2.510 billion crowns.

The analysts foresaw an average full year net profit for the partially privatised group of 3.233 billion crowns, compared to 1995's 3.494 billion crowns. These forecasts ranged from 2.926 to 3.767 billion crowns (Corrects from "forecasts ranged from 4.450 to 5.245 billion crowns").
